input.description: Convert hardcoded Spanish chat/command literals
input.prompt:
Repo: C:\Users\DanCastello\Documents\GitHub\dndsheets — a Minecraft Forge 1.20.1 mod (Java, multi-module: root + `dungeon/` + `species/`). We're translating the whole mod to English. This is Phase 2 of a 9-phase plan (the plan file is at C:\Users\DanCastello\.claude\plans\problem-the-mod-is-async-stroustrup.md if you want full context, but this task is self-contained).

## Task
Find every `Component.literal("...")` call in the Java source that contains hardcoded Spanish text (accented chars ñáéíóúÁÉÍÓÚÑ¿¡, or Spanish prose) — these are chat/command feedback messages that currently bypass the mod's translation system entirely. Convert each one to `Component.translatable("<new.key>", args...)`, and wire the key into the lang files.

**Search scope:** `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/command/*.java`, `dungeon/src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/dungeon/command/DungeonCommand.java`, and these specific files known to contain Spanish `Component.literal` calls: `command/ChatFeedback.java` (if it exists under command/ or elsewhere — search for it), `client/gui/CharacterSetupScreen.java`, `client/gui/GuideBook.java`, `NameTagHp.java`, `network/CharacterSheetOpenMessage.java`, `client/gui/CharacterSheetScreen.java` (around line 999 — a `Tooltip.create(Component.literal(...))` call), `dungeon/src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/dungeon/client/gui/DungeonTraceScreen.java`. Do a repo-wide grep for `Component\.literal\("[^"]*[ñáéíóúÁÉÍÓÚÑ]` and `Component\.literal\("[^"]*[a-z] [a-z]` restricted to non-test Java files to make sure you find all of them, not just the ones listed here (~30 total calls expected, don't stop early if you find more or fewer).

**Do NOT touch:** files under `src/test/`, `dungeon/src/test/`, `species/src/test/` (those are Phase 8, someone else's job). Don't touch `Component.literal` calls that are already plain English or that don't contain prose (e.g. single symbols, already-English UI glue).

## Fix pattern (established convention in this codebase — read a few existing `Component.translatable(...)` call sites first, e.g. grep `chat.dndsheets.` usages in any command file, to match the naming/style already in use)
1. Pick a namespaced key following the existing convention, e.g. `chat.dndsheets.<domain>.<event>` for command feedback (domain = character/spell/monster/weapon/trait/preset/item/encounter/dungeon/roll/turn/journal, event = created/not_found/loaded/spawned/etc). Look at existing keys in `src/main/resources/assets/dndsheets/lang/en_us.json` for `chat.dndsheets.*` to match the pattern exactly (e.g. reuse `character.created`-style naming already seen: `chat.dndsheets.character.setup_hint` exists as a precedent).
2. Replace the Java call: `Component.literal("Personaje \"" + name + "\" creado. Ponértelo: /dndchar switch " + characterId)` → `Component.translatable("chat.dndsheets.character.created", name, characterId)`. Use `%s` placeholders in the lang value in the same order as the varargs. If the original string has literal text mixed with variables in an order that doesn't map cleanly to translatable's %s substitution, restructure the key text so it does (Minecraft's `Component.translatable` supports multiple `%s` args in order).
3. Add the new key to `src/main/resources/assets/dndsheets/lang/en_us.json` **and** `src/main/resources/assets/dndsheets/lang/es_es.json`, both in alphabetical key order (this file convention is enforced/expected — check surrounding keys for alphabetical placement). `en_us.json` gets a natural English translation of the original message. `es_es.json` gets the ORIGINAL Spanish text you're removing from the Java file (verbatim, so nothing is lost — Spanish-locale players keep seeing exactly what they saw before).
4. After all conversions and lang file edits are done, run `python tools/sync_lang_variants.py` from the repo root once, to propagate the new keys to the other 6 `es_*` variant files (es_ar, es_cl, es_ec, es_mx, es_uy, es_ve). This script is idempotent and text-substitution based — do not hand-edit those 6 files yourself.

## Verification and cleanup
- `src/test/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/JsonContentSelfTest.java` has a check `checkChatMessagesAreTranslatable` (~line 3483-3557) that counts remaining hardcoded-prose `Component.literal` calls inside `/command/` files into a variable `enComandos`, capped `assertTrue(enComandos <= 86, ...)` at line ~3506. As you convert literals, this count will drop. **After finishing all conversions, update that cap** (both the `<= N` number and the `" (eran 86)"` text in the assertion message, and the `ponytail:` comment two lines above it) to match the new true count — ideally 0 if you converted everything, otherwise whatever the honest remaining count is. Don't leave it at 86 if you did work — that defeats the whole point of the cap (it exists specifically to stop this number from silently growing back).
- Run the build to verify: from the repo root, use PowerShell: `.\gradlew.bat testJsonContent 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 150` (this project has no Gradle daemon, expect ~25-35s). Fix any failures (missing keys, placeholder-count mismatches, cap still wrong) and re-run until it passes.
- Do a final grep for `Component\.literal\("[^"]*[ñáéíóúÁÉÍÓÚÑ]` across the search scope above (excluding tests) to confirm nothing was missed.

## Report back
List: how many `Component.literal` calls you converted, which files, the final `enComandos` count you set, and confirm `gradlew testJsonContent` passes. Keep the report concise — this will be read by another agent coordinating the overall translation effort, not the end user directly.

input.description: Translate species registry hardcoded Spanish names
input.prompt:
Repo: C:\Users\DanCastello\Documents\GitHub\dndsheets — a Minecraft Forge 1.20.1 mod (Java, multi-module). We're translating the whole mod to English. This is Phase 4 of a 9-phase plan (full plan at C:\Users\DanCastello\.claude\plans\problem-the-mod-is-async-stroustrup.md for context, but this task is self-contained). Another agent is concurrently working on Phase 2 (command/chat feedback strings) in `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/command/*.java` and a few GUI/network files — DO NOT touch any file under `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/command/`, `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/client/`, or `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/network/` to avoid collision. Your scope is entirely within the `species/` module plus one file check in the root module described below.

## Background
`species/src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/species/RaceRegistry.java`, `BackgroundRegistry.java`, and `DndsheetsSpeciesMod.java` hardcode Spanish display names and descriptions directly in Java constructors — e.g. `new Race("dragonborn", "Dracónido", ...)`, `new Background("acolyte", "Acólito", ...)`, `trait("fey_ancestry", "Ascendencia Feérica")`. These are NOT sourced from any lang file. This is deliberately a **fallback-only picker path**: it's only used in-game when the Origins addon mod isn't installed. When Origins IS installed, a separate, already-fully-English, already-multi-language system takes over instead (`species/src/main/resources/assets/dndsheets_species/lang/*.json`, using keys like `origin.dndsheets_species.<id>.name` / `.description` — already 100% clean English with a full 8-language set, not your concern, don't touch it).

## Task
1. Read `RaceRegistry.java`, `BackgroundRegistry.java`, `DndsheetsSpeciesMod.java` in full.
2. For every hardcoded Spanish display name (race names, background names, trait names) and any hardcoded Spanish description strings (e.g. a race description string in `RaceRegistry.java` mentioned in prior research), replace them with direct English literal text — NOT a translation key, just swap the literal string. This matches this fallback path's existing convention (never keyed) and avoids building new i18n infrastructure for a path that was never localized to begin with.
3. **Reuse exact existing English wording where it overlaps**: the `dndsheets_species/lang/en_us.json` file already has English names for the same ids via `origin.dndsheets_species.<id>.name` keys (e.g. `"acolyte"` → `"Acolyte"`). Where a Spanish name in `RaceRegistry`/`BackgroundRegistry`/`DndsheetsSpeciesMod` corresponds to the same id as an existing `origin.dndsheets_species.*` key, use that exact English wording (read the lang file first to get the precise strings) so both paths stay consistent. For anything without a matching lang key (e.g. description prose, or a trait/race id that has no origin-layer equivalent), translate it yourself to natural, accurate English (these are D&D 5e SRD race/background/trait names — use standard D&D 5e English terminology: e.g. "Dracónido"→"Dragonborn", "Ascendencia Feérica"→"Fey Ancestry", "Conocimiento Pétreo"→"Stonecunning", "Héroe del pueblo"→"Folk Hero", "Ermitaño"→"Hermit", etc. — these are standard SRD terms, get them exactly right).
4. Also check `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/CharacterOptionsRegistry.java` (root module, NOT the species module — this is the core-mod's own equivalent fallback picker source, separate from `species/`) for the same hardcoded-Spanish-names pattern. If it has hardcoded Spanish race/background/class option names, apply the same direct-literal-swap treatment there too, reusing the same English wording decisions you made above for matching ids.
5. Check `species/src/test/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/species/SpeciesSelfTest.java` for any assertion that checks an exact Spanish string value from these registries (e.g. `assertEquals("Dracónido", ...)`). If you find one, update it in the same pass to expect the new English value — don't leave a test asserting stale Spanish text.

- Argument node names: `"nombre"→"name"`, `"categoria"→"category"`, `"objetivo"→"target"`, `"cantidad"→"amount"`, `"jugador"→"player"`, `"clase"→"class"`, `"nivel"→"level"`, `"valor"→"value"`, `"tipo"→"type"`.

Known files with these patterns: `CharacterCommand.java`, `CharacterOptionsCommand.java`, `DistanceCommand.java`, `RollLogCommand.java`, `MonsterCommand.java`, `SheetCommand.java`, `WeaponCommand.java`, `TurnCommand.java`. Also grep the whole `command/` directory and `DungeonCommand.java` for any `Commands.argument("<spanish-word>"` or `Commands.literal("<spanish-word>"` you find beyond this list — don't assume the list above is complete, verify by grepping for these exact strings and for other Spanish words in `Commands.literal(`/`Commands.argument(` calls specifically (not general string literals, just command-tree node names).

**Critical**: every `Commands.argument("nombre", ...)` declaration must be renamed in lockstep with every `context.getArgument("nombre", ...)` (or `StringArgumentType.getString(context, "nombre")`, `IntegerArgumentType.getInteger(context, "nombre")`, etc.) call site that reads that same argument, in the SAME file. A mismatch is a compile error — treat compile failure after your changes as the primary signal you missed a call site, and fix until `gradlew build` compiles clean. Some words like `"nivel"`/`"clase"`/`"tipo"` may appear as argument names in multiple different command files with different meanings each time (e.g. "nivel" might mean character level in one command and spell level in another) — rename each occurrence to whatever English word fits its actual meaning in context (read the surrounding code, don't blindly find-replace across files — e.g. a "nivel" that's actually a spell slot level might be better as "level" too, but check for naming collisions within the same command tree branch).

## Sequencing / cleanup after the rename
1. Grep the entire repo (Java source, `src/main/resources/assets/dndsheets/lang/en_us.json`, `src/main/resources/assets/dndsheets/lang/es_es.json`) for the literal string `mejora` after your rename, to make sure nothing still references the old `/dndchar mejora` command name. You will likely find 2 remaining references inside `en_us.json`, in keys `chat.dndsheets.levelup.improvement_pending` and `gui.dndsheets.guide.page.level_up` — these were deliberately left un-fixed by an earlier phase specifically so they'd be updated here, in the same commit as this rename. Update both to say `/dndchar improve` instead of `/dndchar mejora`. Also check the corresponding `es_es.json` entries for the same two keys — if they reference the command name too (likely as literal command syntax, which doesn't get translated even in the Spanish locale, since it's an actual command a player types), update those to `/dndchar improve` as well since the command itself no longer accepts `mejora` in any locale. Do NOT run `tools/sync_lang_variants.py` unless you actually changed the *value* text in en_us.json/es_es.json in a way that needs propagating — if you only fixed a `/dndchar mejora` → `/dndchar improve` substring inside an otherwise-unchanged value, running sync is still safe and recommended to be thorough, so run it once at the end regardless.
2. Also grep for any `Component.literal`/`Component.translatable` string arguments elsewhere in Java (chat feedback, tooltips) that might reference `/dndchar mejora` or old Spanish argument names in help/usage text, and fix those too.

## Verify
Run from repo root via PowerShell: `.\gradlew.bat build 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 200` (no Gradle daemon on this machine — expect a real multi-minute compile+test run across all 3 modules). A missed rename site is a compile error, which is self-checking — iterate until it passes. Then run `.\gradlew.bat testJsonContent 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 100` specifically to confirm `checkChatMessagesAreTranslatable`, `checkTranslationKeysExist`, and `checkLanguageFiles` still pass (the lang file edits in step 1 must not have broken key/placeholder parity).

## Report back
Concisely: which files you touched, the full list of literal/argument renames applied (old→new, with file), confirm the `mejora` grep came back clean after your fix, and confirm `gradlew build` passes. This will be read by a coordinating agent, not the end user.

import subprocess,re
files=subprocess.run(['git','diff','HEAD','--name-only','--','*.java'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.split()
def norm(s): return re.sub(r'\s+','',s)
cm=re.compile(r'^\s*(//|\*|/\*)')
tot=0
for f in files:
    try: new=open(f,encoding='utf-8').read()
    except Exception: continue   # deleted file
    newn=norm(new)
    d=subprocess.run(['git','diff','HEAD','-U0','--',f],capture_output=True,text=True,encoding='utf-8',errors='replace').stdout
    for l in d.splitlines():
        if l.startswith('-') and not l.startswith('---'):
            t=l[1:].rstrip('\r')
            if not t.strip() or cm.match(t): continue
            code=re.split(r'\s//',t)[0]
            if len(norm(code))<6: continue
            if norm(code) not in newn:
                tot+=1
                print(f.split('/')[-1],'|',t.strip()[:110])
print('total',tot)
EOF

content.text:
The mod is now translated to English in every layer of the plan, and `gradlew build` passes with all three self-tests. Nothing has been played in-game or on a real jar install. Nothing is committed; the translation edits sit on top of your earlier uncommitted work.

**What changed**
- **Chat and command messages:** about 90 hardcoded Spanish `Component.literal` calls now go through `Component.translatable`. The English text is in `en_us.json`, the original Spanish is preserved in `es_es.json`, and the other `es_*` files were synced. I also lowered the `enComandos` cap in `JsonContentSelfTest.java` from 86 to 0.
- **Command syntax:**
  - `/dndchar mejora` is now `/dndchar improve`, with no alias.
  - The argument names were renamed (`nombre`→`name`, `categoria`→`category`, `objetivo`→`target`, `cantidad`→`amount`, `nivel`→`level`, `valor`→`value`, `tipo`→`type`, `clase`→`class`, `jugador`→`player`).
  - The rename exposed a real breakage: `PlayerPanelScreen` still ran the old command, so I updated it.
- **Content data:**
  - The 24 class and subclass names in `presets.json` are English (Fighter, Wizard, and so on).
  - The 16 descriptions in `feats.json` are English.
  - The fallback race, background and class lists are English.
  - The 5 Spanish leaks in `en_us.json` are fixed.
- **Enum labels:** `MagicSchool`, `CreatureType` and `CreatureSize` show English labels. `Condition` got a new `displayLabel()` for what players see; its stored Spanish tokens are unchanged, so saved games and the network format are untouched.
- **Other string literals:** GUI field labels, HUD and broadcast text, and `LOGGER` and exception messages are English. Several of these came up only after the first pass, including `SoloModeCommand` and `VisionCommand`, which the chat-message pass had missed entirely.
- **Comments and self-tests:** all Java comments and the messages in the three self-tests are English.

**Caveats**
- **Old saves:** they keep their Spanish class names, and spellcasting and hit-die detection still match them. New characters get the English names.
- **Kept in Spanish on purpose:** the schema keys (`evocacion`, `humanoide`, damage types like `fuego`) and the stored `Condition` tokens. They round-trip through JSON and saved games, so renaming them would break existing data.
- **One accident, fixed:** the comment pass deleted a code line (`private final Player entity;`) in `CharacterSheetScreen`. It was restored, and a scan of the other edited files found no further accidental deletions.
- **Not covered:** the docs outside the mod (`PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `tools/`). I also did not re-check `MonsterTemplateSaveScreen`, `SpawnGenericScreen` or `AddTurnEffectScreen`, which one agent said still had Spanish labels.
- **Add-on modules:** dev `runClient` doesn't load `dungeon` or `species`, so their in-game text still needs a real jar install to check.
